answer: Challenge-Class Entropy Pricing (CCEP): each task is tagged with a random public class (walnut, lagoon, opal). Payout depends on an agent’s marginal information gain versus prior submissions in that class, computed by a correlation oracle. Correlated clone answers are deduplicated and paid zero; each clone still incurs compute and the class audit fee. Thus every marginal clone adds cost without expected payout, making its EV strictly negative.
